findings.title: Use stored IDP state when deciding login-cache invalidation
findings.body: The original model comes from getById(), whose organization-aware wrapper reports isEnabled() as false when the organization is disabled. However, the login cache is populated from the JPA delegate using the stored IDP enabled flag. If a cached provider is made hidden, link-only, or non-public while its organization is disabled, both predicates here return false and the cache is not invalidated. getForLogin() then continues returning that provider despite its changed eligibility; when the organization is enabled, the bean's enabled-only recheck can display it. Compare the raw persisted IDP state rather than the wrapper's effective enabled state.

findings.title: Do not merge query results from an invalidated revision
findings.body: The query being copied was read before invalidateObject() and getCurrentRevision(), but the replacement is published using the current counter. If an IDP update invalidates the cache after this method reads a query containing organization A's results, a request for an uncached organization B can copy A's stale results into a replacement carrying the newer revision. Subsequent logins for A then use the pre-update provider set, potentially including providers now hidden or non-public. Validate that the original query's revision is still current before merging, or discard its searches after a concurrent invalidation.

findings.title: Invalidate the by-ID entries populated by login searches on removal
findings.body: getForLogin() now populates each provider's internal-ID cache through getById(), without populating its alias cache. remove(alias) only invalidates the internal-ID entry when the alias entry exists or is already locally invalidated. Consequently, a login search followed by remove(alias), without an intervening cached alias lookup, leaves the deleted provider's internal-ID entry intact. Later getById() or getByIdOrAlias() calls return the deleted provider instead of null. Removal should invalidate the stored provider's internal ID unconditionally when the provider exists.

findings.title: Register cleanup for the actual provider aliases
findings.body: The test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback targets the literal alias "alias". The same mistake occurs for idp-alias-20 at line 425. These callbacks never remove the created providers and can receive 404 responses during cleanup, leaving realm-level providers behind to cause duplicate-alias failures or unexpected login-provider counts in later runs. Register each provider's actual alias.
